notes.text: Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 173:18 together.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 48% of the team’s power-play time in 14 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 30% last season.
Anthony Mantha is day to day, reported after he played in their last game.
Connor Hellebuyck joined from WPG on Oct 24.

stakes: The Oilers go in first in the Pacific with 22 points, the Devils second in the Metropolitan with 18 points.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Devils (9-5-0) beat Vegas 5-2 on Friday. The Oilers have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of the Islanders. Going in, the Oil are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth).

The Oilers’ record (.786) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.625), largely thanks to their finishing. The Devils have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .741, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). They also have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st), and their power play against the Devils’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Edmonton has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. The Devils keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). That means the Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 29 A / 37 P in 14 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 14 A / 26 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Arseny Gritsyuk (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Tristan Jarry (4-1-2 / .895 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for Edmonton, and Jake Allen (5-3-0 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) for New Jersey.
